title: Should `results.tbl` rows be sorted?
body:
nail writes each row of `results.tbl` as an alignment thread finishes it. Within a query, rows are not in E-value or score order; a survey of `dev` on 2026-11-02 saw 8.1e-32 above 5.5e-34. At more than one thread the order also changes between runs (memory `results-tbl-row-order-varies-with-threads`). The root README's example shows sorted rows.

## Options

- Sort each query's rows by E-value. nail would have to hold a query's rows until all its seeds are done.
- Sort the whole file at the end of the run. That holds every row in memory or rereads the file.
- Leave the order as it is and say in the README that it is unordered.

I lean to documenting the order for now. Sorting costs memory on large searches.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/69ba1bc3
notes.text:
Jack chose sorting per query block, and wants a later switch for very large searches where holding a query's hits costs memory. Two designs were tried on 2026-11-02 and rejected before commit.

The first kept, in `OutputStage`, a count of seeds left per query and a held `Vec<PipelineResult>` per query, filled from the seeds after seeding, and wrote a query's hits sorted when its count reached zero. Rejected as too much machinery.

The second kept one `Vec<PipelineResult>` buffer in `OutputStage`, flushed sorted whenever a result for a different query arrived, with a `finish` call after the loop. Under threads, chunks of 100 seeds from different queries interleave, so a query's block splits into sorted sub-blocks. Rejected for that.

Both needed `OutputStage::run` to take its results by value, since `PipelineResult` and `Alignment` are not `Clone`, and `Stats::add_sample` to split so the per-result part runs before output. Any design that holds results meets the same two points.

The sort was last present before commit `38ab2fd`, where it ran per chunk of 100 seeds.
